segments.t: Welcome to Season Six of Kukhnya! Today Hotel Eleon is hosting the lavish wedding of owner Eleonora Andreyevna and showman Dmitry Nagiyev, and Eleonora is already grilling restaurant director Ilya over the VIP seating plan.
За нашим столиком будет сидеть олигарх.
Подождите, у нас столик на четверых.
Вы у нас директор ресторана, Илья.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
За нашим столиком будет сидеть олигарх.
'An oligarch will be sitting at our table.' Even though an oligarch will be sitting at their table, Eleonora keeps a steady face in front of Ilya.
'They called and will definitely come.' Admitting that they called and will definitely come shows Ilya being honest for a change.
Подождите, у нас столик на четверых.

'Wait, our table is for four.' Saying that their table is for four is how Ilya sets the tone with Eleonora. In Russian you say "by me" or "with us" rather than "I have", so the situation sits right with the person.
'And you end up with six people.' Between the plan and the wedding, Ilya gives Eleonora a quick, grounded response.
'You tell me how to do it.' Adding that Ilya tells her how to do it fills in the missing piece for Ilya. Notice how she sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
Вы у нас директор ресторана, Илья.

'You are our restaurant director, Ilya.' Saying that Ilya is their restaurant director Ilya is how Eleonora sets the tone with Ilya. In Russian you say "by me" or "with us" rather than "I have", so the situation sits right with the person.
'Yes, alright.' With the kitchen and wedding in play, Ilya keeps this short reply brisk and direct.
'Eleonora Andreyevna, sorry to interrupt.' Around the kitchen and wedding, Ilya sets a calm, everyday tone with Eleonora.

'Here, they brought your dress.' Ilya reminds Eleonora that here they brought Eleonora's dress before the moment passes. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
'And Dmitry Vladimirovich's tailcoat.' Between the kitchen and the wedding, Ilya gives Eleonora a quick, grounded response.

'Let's go through the wedding script.' Noting that they should go through the wedding script keeps Eleonora's side of the story simple and clear. Starting with "davay" is the everyday Russian way to say "come on, let us do this".

'Make it faster, okay?' With the restaurant and conversation hanging in the air, Eleonora puts Ilya on the spot. In Russian, she does not need helper words like "do" or "did"—rising pitch alone turns it into a question. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
За нашим столиком будет сидеть олигарх.
Подождите, у нас столик на четверых.
Вы у нас директор ресторана, Илья.
With the wedding dress delivered and the VIP table overcrowded, the pressure on the hotel staff is already sky-high. Until next time!
